etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English capcious, from Middle French captieux, or its source, Latin captiōsus, from captiō.
senses: (obsolete) That captures; especially, (of an argument, words etc.) designed to capture or entrap in misleading arguments; sophistical.
Having a disposition to find fault unreasonably or to raise petty objections; cavilling, nitpicky.
